notes: Coders matched closely (all three document stances agreed). Disagreements: (1) granularity, where one coder merged or split a sentence (syllabus statement vs discussion at start of term, help-seeking sentence, CS handbook syllabus pointer, administrative-transparency clause); resolved by splitting when the source gives two distinct actions and dropping duplicates of one rule. (2) modality and unit_stance for recommendation-style language (should-not vs must-not on detectors, informs vs should for resource pointers, require vs neutral for transparency expectations); resolved from the verb in the source and the section it sits in. (3) policy_type, e.g. P09 vs P66 for clarifying expectations (no syllabus mentioned, so P66) and P77 vs P36 for the CS handbook's 'follows university rules' (P77). (4) Actor/phase for the instructor-decides sentence (instructor, before-course). Seven units found only by A and five of seven found only by B were kept after checking the text; two B units (a duplicate help-seeking unit, and a description of the research-guide's contents) were dropped as duplicate or not a policy statement.
